name: Ong's Hat
title: The Ghost Town With a Door to Another Earth
claims: Ong's Hat is described as one of the earliest Internet-based secret history conspiracy theories | 1
It was created as collaborative fiction by four core individuals dating back to the 1980s, with membership changing over time | 1
It is often cited as the first alternate reality game on many ARG lists | 1
The characters were largely based in the ghost town of Ong's Hat, New Jersey, which gave the project its name | 1
The story's threads trace back to the 1980s on bulletin board systems, mail art networks, early zines and faxlore | 1
The story eventually used print, radio, television and digital media (CD-ROM, DVD, Internet, BBS) | 1
It may have started as an in-joke, an early ARG, transmedia storytelling, a memetic experiment, or a combination | 1
The tale may be based on earlier works | 1
Ground rules acknowledged the experiment could go down darker paths and specifically ruled out cult-like activity | 1
The project was eventually concluded by its author | 1
GamesTM wrote that Ong's Hat was more an experiment in transmedia storytelling than a modern ARG, but its DNA is evident in every ARG that came after | 1
In 2002 Lego created an ARG for its toys for the Canadian children's TV series Galidor: Defenders of the Outer Dimension that featured some Ong's Hat elements | 1
The narrative concerns renegade Princeton professors doing quantum physics and chaos theory experiments on dimensional travel with a device called "the egg" | 1

The story is introduced through two documents, Incunabula: A Catalog of Rare Books, Manuscripts & Curiosa, Conspiracy Theory, Frontier Science & Alternative Worlds and Ong's Hat: Gateway to the Dimensions | 1, 2
The story is said to begin in 1978 when Wali Fard bought over 200 acres of forested land and set up an ashram | 1
The ashram was for seekers of spirituality, politics, tantra and psychopharmacology, and hosted Princeton physicists and other accredited scientists doing interdimensional experiments | 1
It was rumored they were trying to train the human mind to manipulate quantum physics and reality | 1
The Egg was developed in the late 1980s as a variation of a sensory deprivation chamber, used to help determine when a wave becomes a particle | 1
During a test the Egg disappeared; a young man inside said that in the seven minutes it was gone he traveled to another dimension of Earth, identical but without human life | 1
When military efforts threatened the research, the ashram was moved piece by piece to the other Earth, leaving only the house with the gateway; residents return only to restock supplies | 1

The documents describe a Pine Barrens similar to ours in a world that never developed human life, called "our first Newfoundland," with weather-grey shacks, airstream trailers, recycled chicken coops and mail order yurts, more spread out and relaxed | 2
The setting is the New Jersey Pine Barrens | 2
The meme blended quantum physics, tantric sex, chaos magick, parallel universes and conspiracy theory and spread through the noosphere over about a decade | 2
It reached Coast to Coast AM and Jane Magazine and was the starting point for the ARG Chasing the Wish | 2
The author of Ong's Hat: The Beginning is described as the author of the only book on the subject | 2
He called the Incunabula catalog a culture jam, said no group existed previous to 1987 as described, and that 4 people got together in the 80s and 90s and put the documents together | 2
He said they took pre-existing fiction bits, current pop science and parody of paranormal conspiracy literature and graffitied it on the walls of the noosphere | 2
He said legends and synchronicities have occurred since, which he called beautiful and indicative of a responsive universe | 2

Three of the creators made a verbal pact: never use it to start a cult, never trample those who worked on it, give away any money if more accessible channels made money, and toss it into the public domain via a free game if it became too much; the third completed the mission, called stage 3, "Done" | 2

He described two camps: a majority who see it as a joke, including creators who put out installments 5 and 6 to re-inject levity, and a vocal minority of "believers" he accused of deceit and denial and of building a "cockeyed religion" | 2

He gave an "OTHER answer (cue spooky music)" claiming a black-budget contract after MKULTRA's exposure to cultural engineers, producing the Incunabula as an addictive, circular design ending in madness, "a virtual asylum that the inmates willingly enter," with Attract/Entrap/Entrain | 2
He said that if you read this and continue, it is testament to the robustness of the design | 2

He described the Metamachine as an upgrade of earlier works, inspired by a novel read early in life, using relational databases to access metadata of human knowledge, with results he was still interpreting and a redesign around distributed computing | 2
He said the mind control subculture is mostly people seeking a cop-out or manipulating others for profit, ego and power | 2
The interview was archived in 2006 | 2
A 1984 interview at Princeton University includes references to an origin of the legend | 1
Further reading lists Ong's Hat books from 1999 and 2002, a 2011 book on legend-tripping online and the search for Ong's Hat, and Ong's Hat: Compleat in 2025 | 1
